evidence.text: The street already sits at the floor of the FY guide: Autoliv's own 2026-10-19 consensus (20 analysts) has FY2026 adj. EBIT margin at 10.4% against the company's 'around 10.5-11%' range, and Q4 at 13.9% (range 12.5-15.0%) where the guide midpoint needs roughly 15%; so a narrowing of the FY range to 'around 10.5%' at this print matches consensus, holding the full range would beat it, and only a cut below 10.5% is a new negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: At Q2 (2026-07-17) the company kept the FY range but back-loaded it into Q4 and the stock fell 3.78% (baseline); at Q3 2025 it kept its FY margin guide and the stock fell 2.62%; the Q1 prints that rose (+6.82%, +5.56%) were the ones where the guide was first reassured.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partly priced by construction: the consensus IS the market's bar. What is not priced is the asymmetry: if the market feared a cut below 10.5%, the 25d skew would be put-paid and short interest would have kept building into October; instead the skew is -2.83 (upside paid) and the stock rose 4.7% in five sessions.
evidence.independence: The Q2 transcript (https://www.autoliv.com/sites/autoliv/files/pr/Autoliv_Q2_2026_webcast_transcript.pdf, 2026-07-17) shows the CEO declined to bias the range to either half and Wells Fargo computed ~15% Q4 needed for the midpoint, i.e. the street was told the Q4 step-up depends on raw-material compensation and engineering income. evidence.text: OPmobility (European exterior/module supplier) cut its 2026 operating-margin target from ~EUR500M to EUR430-450M on 2026-10-07, citing S&P Global Mobility's September production forecast cuts (especially China), European customers scaling back, and persistent raw-material/component inflation tied to the Middle East; its shares fell ~19.6% and dragged the sector - the same two drivers (volumes and Gulf-linked raw materials) Autoliv said its back-loaded Q4 and the $110M raw-material headwind depend on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Autoliv's Q2 2026 print, where the raw-material headwind and the Q4 back-loading were first disclosed, cost 3.78% on the day.
evidence.why_not_priced: Peer warnings are visible, so this is at most half unpriced: ALV has risen 4.7% in five sessions and 3.1% in twenty since, with upside skew, so the market is not treating OPmobility's raw-material read-across as a threat to Autoliv's Q4 compensation; if it were, ALV would have de-rated after 2026-10-08 and the skew would be put-paid.
evidence.independence: Proxy: different products and a far larger European mix than Autoliv (EMEA 30% of ALV sales). Valeo's 2026-10-22 release (separate finding) says challenges 'have intensified over recent months'. evidence.text: Valeo's Q3 2026 sales, published 2026-10-22: group -2.6% like-for-like, original equipment -3.8% lfl in an automotive market Valeo puts at -1.6%, FY targets confirmed, CEO saying challenges 'have intensified over recent months'; the stock fell about 4% on the day.

evidence.text: AppFolio's FY2026 revenue guide ($1.117-1.127B, raised twice from an initial $1.100-1.120B) less H1 actuals ($262.0M + $281.1M = $543.1M) implies H2 revenue of $573.9-583.9M, i.e. 15.4-17.4% growth over H2 2025 ($249.35M + $248M), against 19% printed in Q2 and 20% in Q1; applying last year's Q2-to-Q3 sequential step (+5.8%) to Q2 gives ~$297M for Q3, about 1% above the $294.2M consensus, which would leave room for a fourth consecutive FY raise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raises have been bought unevenly: Q2 2026 beat + raise +0.67%; Q1 2026 raise +11.16%; Q3 2025 revenue beat 1.5% + raise (EPS miss) +7.94%; Q4 2025 initial FY26 guide -8.31% (baseline history).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: street FY revenue (~$1.12B) sits at the guide midpoint, so a raise is the expected habit rather than a surprise, and the call-heavy open interest and negative skew show the market already leans up. What is not priced is the size of the H2 cushion: if the street had modelled a ~$297M Q3 the consensus would read ~$297M, not $294.2M. Q2 also guided to 'a more moderate pace of unit expansion among existing customers', which the conservative H2 implies but may over-discount.
evidence.independence: Initial guide and Q1 guide from the company's own releases: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1433195/000143319526000006/appfq42025exhibit991.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000021/appfq12026exhibit991.htm (same issuer, so one line of evidence). Resident Onboarding Lift and LiveEasy move-in services management named as growth drivers).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release isolates this line; VAS growth has held at ~22% for Q1 and Q2 2026 through a flat-rent market, and the stock reacted to the headline and guide rather than to leasing activity.
evidence.why_not_priced: A sector series that sell-side previews rarely tie to AppFolio's transaction revenue; if priced, Q3 estimates would sit below the seasonal run-rate rather than at ~18% growth. Proxy only: multifamily-weighted, and AppFolio skews to single-family and small multifamily.
evidence.independence: Proxy. AppFolio's own Q2 remarks flagged 'a more moderate pace of unit expansion among existing customers' (https://www.webull.com/news/15278807508870144). Cuts against it: the broader single-family rent series is accelerating (next finding). Short interest 7% of float / 8.65 days to cover shrinks this negative.

evidence.text: Cotality's Single-Family Rent Index rose 2.0% y/y in August 2026, up from 1.8% in July and 1.5% in June, the sixth straight month of faster annual growth; with units on platform +8% y/y, rent payment volume through AppFolio Payments (the largest VAS line) would grow about 10% in Q3, a little faster than in H1.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated in any past release; payments sits inside VAS, which grew 22% in Q1 and Q2 2026.
evidence.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed; consensus at ~18% Q3 growth sits close to the H1 run-rate, which does not suggest an acceleration in rent volume is modelled. Small because it is a proxy and the rent effect is a few tenths of a point of revenue growth.

If the market had fully priced a recovery to anywhere near the Q3 2024 level ($321.6M), the stock would sit well above the ~$29 average target.

evidence.text: A reaffirmation of the 2026 guide is close to arithmetically assured. On FCF, H1 was about C$1.8bn (Q2 C$982m) against a C$4.1-4.3bn guide, so H2 needs C$2.3-2.5bn. Management said capex runs at about C$550m a quarter in H2 (Q2: C$695m) and that FCF growth 'further accelerates in the second half'. The market's expectation is a reaffirmation. A narrowing to the upper half is possible on revenue and EBITDA; FCF is the line that could disappoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was reaffirmed on 2026-07-22 and the stock still fell: -3.1% pre-market (RTTNews) and -4.13% per the baseline. evidence.independence: The company guide is from the 2026-08-05 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000106040/000162828026053305/a4ex991-pressreleaseq426.htm); the August reaction to a beat with an above-consensus guide is reported at https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/western-digital-tops-estimates-offers-204900191.html.

evidence.text: Toshiba plans to roughly double its AI data-center HDD capacity by fiscal 2027 (~JPY60bn, about $380M, in the Philippines; medium-term capacity-share goal about 30% from just over 10%), per Nikkei on 2026-10-02. That day WDC fell about 10%. UBS's Arcuri says hyperscalers plan to push as much volume as they can to Toshiba. The call will be asked whether this changes LTA pricing for 2029-31, which management said in August was still being negotiated.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Commentary-driven: the 2026-10-02 report alone moved WDC -10.2%. There is no prior print where competitor capacity was the question.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the main wire narrative for the October selloff. What remains is the management answer on LTA pricing. If the market had fully absorbed it, UBS and Wells would not still be framing customer-contract talks as the open question for the call.
evidence.independence: Analysis noting the plan names no customer commitments (https://letsdatascience.com/news/toshiba-plans-to-double-hdd-capacity-for-ai-data-centers-3b445b0f) cuts the other way; Wells Fargo calls the concern 'misunderstood' (https://finance.biggo.com/news/2fa93fdb-e4c6-4ef2-b9c6-cf4f433f2c80). evidence.text: Gross-margin expansion is decelerating. The Q1 GM guide of 55-56% is only +60 to +160bp over Q4's 54.4%, against +390bp from Q3 (50.5%) to Q4. At Citi the CFO said DRAM and NAND input costs are a headwind to cost-per-TB declines and that WDC is 'in between two product transitions' (40TB ePMR ramping, HAMR not until 1H CY27). Memory prices kept rising: TrendForce saw DRAM contract +13-18% in Jul-Sep, and Micron guided its November quarter to $61.5B against $57.0B consensus on 2026-09-30. That raises the risk of a modest December GM guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: the Q1 GM guide implied a sharply slower margin step-up, and the stock fell -13% despite the beat. The baseline does not isolate which line drove it.
evidence.why_not_priced: The pricing narrative dominates previews; only one preview (Investing.com, 2026-10-22) mentions component inflation, and none quantifies it. If it were priced, the December GM consensus (FY27 GM about 57.6% per data providers) would sit below the CFO's 'pretty good pace'.
evidence.independence: Micron's FQ4 2026 results and guide (https://beancount.io/de/blog/2026/10/02/micron-fy2026-q4-earnings-analysis). The Investing.com preview flags component costs and mix pressuring margins (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/western-digital-faces-earnings-test-as-hdd-pricing-debate-looms-93CH-4966687). It shares the Citi transcript with finding 1. Memory-to-HDD-cost transmission is a proxy beyond the company's own qualitative remark.

evidence.text: Convertible cleanup. On 2026-08-26 WDC exchanged about $191.0M of its 3.00% 2028 converts for ~$192.7M cash plus shares. On 2026-09-14 it called the remaining $109.5M for redemption on 2026-11-16: conversion deadline 2026-11-12, 26.5231 shares per $1,000, principal in cash, the excess in stock over a 40-day averaging period. That is about 2.6M shares, roughly 0.7% of the ~388M share count. The balance sheet is net cash after the Sandisk stake monetization. The money retires debt and funds nothing new, and there is no distress signal; the sign is neutral.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is small and public. The dilution is likely inside the guided ~388M diluted share count, and conversion-arb hedge selling during averaging is modest relative to 9M shares a day.
evidence.independence: 8-K of 2026-08-26 (exchange agreements), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/106040/000119312526365796/0001193125-26-365796.txt

evidence.text: On 2026-09-21 newly appointed CEO John Calmes said in the Ex.99.1 press release that 'through two and a half months of the second fiscal quarter, our business is producing strong results similar to what we reported in the first quarter'. Q1 FY27 was GAAP $1.33 and adjusted $2.12 against a $0.58 bar. The Q2 bar is $0.79. A Q1-like quarter is revenue ~$140M, provision ~$44-48M (Q1 $43.8M; Q2 FY26 $49.8M), G&A ex-one-offs ~$72-74M and interest ~$12M, on ~4.55M diluted shares: roughly $0.85-2.20 EPS.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name's print-day move has followed the EPS-surprise sign on every print in the baseline. Beats: Q1 FY27 (+265% vs est) +13.0%; Q3 FY25 (+99%) +16.3%; Q4 FY25 (+27%) +3.4%. Misses: Q2 FY26 -12.8%, Q1 FY26 -9.6%, Q3 FY26 -17.6%. Q4 FY26, in line, -4.0%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Calmes made the statement in a CEO-appointment release, and the stock fell 6.1% that day on the leadership news, not the business update. Consensus then fell, not rose (Benzinga $1.07 on Sep 4 to $0.78 on Oct 16, snippet), so the one or two analysts are not modelling a Q1-like quarter. If the market had priced it, the bar would be above $1.50 and the stock would have recovered the September drop instead of sitting at $171.
evidence.independence: Q1 FY27 release (separate document) for the base it is 'similar' to: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108385/000143774926024363/ex_992357.htm. Caveat, already netted into the size: 'strong results' may describe credit and operations rather than EPS, and Q2 carries a seasonal allowance build ahead of the Oct-Dec demand peak.

evidence.text: Credit was improving into Q2 and the year-ago comparison is soft. Q1 FY27: NCO 18.2% annualised vs 19.4%, 61+ days delinquency 5.2% vs 5.4%, provision $43.8M vs $50.5M (-13%), after underwriting was tightened around January 2026. Q2 FY26 lost $0.38/share on a $49.8M provision driven by 40% new-customer growth, $6.1M share-based comp, a $3.7M bond-redemption charge and a $1.3M discrete tax item, none of which recur at that size.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Provision drove the Q1 FY27 beat and +13.0% move. The provision and SBC-driven miss in Q2 FY26 brought -12.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.79 implies a provision near Q2 FY26's level despite a smaller new-customer cohort. If it were priced, estimates would sit nearer Q1's run-rate.
evidence.independence: Q1 FY27 metrics come from a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108385/000143774926024363/ex_992357.htm. This finding supports the same EPS line as finding 1 and is sized small to avoid counting the beat twice.

evidence.text: New-customer lending was cut hard and the book is barely growing into peak season. Q1 FY27 new-customer originations were $24.9M vs $41.6M (-40%), customers -1.9% YoY and gross loans +2.3% YoY. Underwriting was 'only modestly loosened' a month before the July call. Q2 FY26 gross loans grew 4.0% QoQ on new customers. A weak Q2 build makes revenue soft against $140.7M (Q1 $139.2M) and dents the forward growth story on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline does not isolate loan growth from EPS. In October 2025 the company showed its first YoY loan growth since 2022 while EPS missed, and the stock fell 12.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is 23% off its high. The Q2 loan balance is new information on the print. Shrunk for the crowded short (6.2 days to cover).
evidence.independence: Call summary (allmind transcript, 2026-07-24): COO says the credit box was tightened six months earlier and is 'still pretty conservative' with 'demand robust'. https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2945474. This is the same lower-growth fact that drives finding 2's lower provision, so the two partly offset by construction.
